sammendrag: This report presents the outcomes of the final evaluation of the Capital Modernisation Fund (CMF) funded UK online centres. The centres were intended to ‘bridge the gap between those in society who have access to information and communications technology (ICT) and are able to use it competently and confidently and those who do not’. The focus of the initiative was on adults in disadvantaged communities with six specified target groups: unemployed people; single parents; people with disabilities; minority ethnic groups; people with basic skills needs; and people over the age of 60 who had not been involved in learning for some time. The initiative was launched in 2000 and by November 2002, 6,000 online centres had been established, over half of these with CMF funding. The evaluation of CMF centres was designed to assess the impact and efficiency of the program as a whole and to identify specifically whether participants increased their ICT skills and the extent to which participants are achieving short- and long-term outcomes as a result of improving their ICT skills and having access to ICT. The study also explored the issue of ‘deadweight’, or activity that would have happened in any case, the extent of deadweight loss, and the broader impact of the centres on individuals and the community in general. The evaluation found that the centres reached the target groups with almost two thirds of those using the centres in one of the six priority target groups. The study did not identify significant levels of ‘deadweight’ and most respondents to the initial user survey (84%) stated that they had learned new skills they would not have acquired otherwise. Many users progress to further learning and employment and over 90% expressed satisfaction with the centres. In terms of overall program impact, the evidence suggests that many centres are not reaching many people in the most excluded groups. In addition, the evidence infers that only those with Internet access at home, work or college have ‘truly crossed the digital divide’. The report makes recommendations for the future of online centres.
tittel: Evaluation of CMF funded UK online centres: final report
